title: Completed affine sections of a power-torsion quasi-coherent sheaf
statement: Let $Y$ be a Noetherian scheme, $J$ an ideal sheaf, $U$ an affine open, $B=\Gamma(Y,U)$, $R=\widehat{B}_{J(U)}$ the completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $g:\operatorname{Spec} R\to Y$ the completion ring map followed by the affine chart inclusion. Let $A$ evaluate module sheaves on $U$, and let $P$ be tensor pullback along $g$ followed by global Spec sections and restriction of scalars along $B\to R$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. There exists a natural transformation $c:A\to P$ such that, for every quasi-coherent module sheaf $M$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every $n\in\mathbb N$ with $J(U)^{n+1}\Gamma(U,M)=0$, $c_M$ is an isomorphism of $B$-modules. This concerns individual sheaves and includes no formal system or diagram transitions.

source.place: Completed base-change paragraph; Tags 05GG (completion quotient) and 01I9 (affine pullback).

proof.text: Define c from the tensor-pullback adjunction unit, restricted to the whole Spec R, which is the inverse image of U. Spec global sections and the affine chart identify the ring action with B → R. Naturality of the unit and restriction gives a natural transformation on all sheaves.

For quasi-coherent M, affine pullback sections identify c_M with m ↦ 1 tensor m. The annihilation assumption factors the B action through B/J(U)^(n+1). The ideal is finitely generated since B is Noetherian, so the completion quotient formula identifies R/J(U)^(n+1)R with B/J(U)^(n+1). Tensoring over this quotient identifies c_M with the identity; hence c_M is invertible.

lean.statement:
theorem completedAffineSections_powerTorsion
    {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian Y] (J : Y.IdealSheafData) (U : Y.affineOpens) :
    let B := Γ(Y, U.1)
    let R := AdicCompletion (J.ideal U) B
    let S := Spec (CommRingCat.of R)
    let g : S ⟶ Y := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap B R)) ≫
      U.2.isoSpec.inv ≫ U.1.ι
    let T := Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback g
    let E := moduleSpecΓFunctor (R := CommRingCat.of R)
    let L := ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap B R)
    ∃ c : SheafOfModules.evaluation Y.ringCatSheaf (op U.1) ⟶ T ⋙ E ⋙ L,
      ∀ (M : Y.Modules) (_ : M.IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℕ),
        J.ideal U ^ (n + 1) • (⊤ : Submodule B Γ(M, U.1)) = ⊥ →
          IsIso (c.app M)
